master.words: A tall young Chinese swordswoman of twenty, black hair gathered in a high bun with a wooden hairpin, a straight serious face, wearing a long pale blue-grey hanfu robe to the ankles with a white inner collar and wide sleeves, a dark blue-grey sash tied at the waist with its ends hanging, dark cloth shoes. She holds a plain straight Chinese jian sword with a brass guard in her right hand. She stands in a martial guard stance: knees slightly bent, weight low, the sword held out forward and level toward the right at chest height, the left hand raised open by her chest. Drawn in soft graphite pencil and light watercolour wash on warm aged paper, in the manner of an old Chinese book illustration, clean confident outlines, gentle shading. The whole figure from the top of the bun to the shoes, seen from the SIDE, facing RIGHT, alone on plain empty paper, no ground, no other objects, no text. Set in old rural China (Ming dynasty dress), not Japanese, not Western.
